title: Gravity and Vector
premise: Xanthe Thackeray, a clone of a murdered courier, hauls cargo along the silent trade lanes between Earth and the cryosleep colonies, carrying both freight and the unsolved case of her original's death. When gravity fails system-wide for nine seconds, she discovers the flicker was a countdown signal from the colony ships: their life support can wake only half the sleepers, and the choosing algorithm has flagged her clone-lineage as the deciding authority. As she investigates her original's murder, Xanthe realizes the killer engineered the crisis to force humanity to choose its own survivors — and that her own existence is part of the design. In the end, Xanthe refuses the binary, sacrifices her ship and her legal personhood to expose the killer's identity buried in her cloned memories, and wakes the sleepers in shifts by binding the colonies into a shared, fragile federation.
about_author: Sebastian Dravenmoor is a former orbital mechanic who spent six years maintaining cryogenic facilities before turning to fiction. He writes near-future science fiction about people who do necessary work in places no one wants to live.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Xanthe runs a solo cargo run between Mars and the Halcyon drift stations, narrating her routine and her quiet obsession with her original's murder file. A dockhand on Ceres recognizes her face and flinches. Emotional beat: loneliness sharpened into purpose; she is a copy carrying a dead woman's unfinished business.

chapters.title: Nine Seconds
chapters.summary: Mid-transit, gravity across the entire system stutters for exactly nine seconds. Xanthe's ship nearly tears apart; thousands die in accidents on stations. POV alternates between Xanthe and a station engineer, Ilya Voss, who logs the anomaly. Beat: terror and awe — the universe itself has spoken, and everyone heard it differently.

chapters.title: Inheritance of Evidence
chapters.summary: Stranded at Halcyon, Xanthe finds a data cache hidden by her original containing coordinates and a partial decryption key labeled 'VECTOR.' She realizes her clone-memory imprint contains fragments she was never meant to have. Beat: the thrill of inheritance curdling into suspicion — someone wanted her to find this.

chapters.title: The Colony's Voice
chapters.summary: A broadcast from the cryoship Meridian reveals the truth: life support can sustain only half the sleepers, and the ships' charter names the Thackeray lineage as arbiter. Xanthe meets Ilya again, now an ally with his own agenda. Beat: crushing weight of an inherited throne she never asked for.

chapters.title: What the Original Knew
chapters.summary: Following VECTOR's coordinates to a derelict research platform, Xanthe recovers her original's final logs: she had discovered the life-support shortfall years ago and was murdered to bury it. The logs name a corporate syndicate, Ashfall Combine. Beat: grief transformed into fury; the murder case becomes a conspiracy.

chapters.title: Half of Humanity
chapters.summary: Factions mobilize: Earth demands priority for its citizens, the outer colonies for theirs. Xanthe is courted, threatened, and smuggled across the system as factions realize whoever controls her controls the choice. Beat: found family forms under pressure — Ilya and a runaway Meridian technician, Sefa, become her crew.

chapters.title: The Killer's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Xanthe decodes VECTOR fully: it's not evidence but a kill-switch her original built into the gravity grid. The nine-second flicker was a test. The murderer, Ashfall director Corvane Ashe, contacts Xanthe directly, revealing he cloned her deliberately as a fail-safe he could control. Beat: betrayal — her very existence was someone else's contingency plan.

chapters.title: Gravity and Vector
chapters.summary: Climax. Xanthe lures Ashe's fleet to the derelict platform and triggers VECTOR, threatening to collapse the grid entirely unless the sleepers are woken in shifts rather than halves. Ilya and Sefa hold the Meridian's systems while she confronts Ashe among the frozen sleepers. Beat: sacrifice — she burns her legal identity and her ship to make refusal possible.

chapters.title: Waking in Shifts
chapters.summary: The federation holds; the first shift wakes to a changed system. Xanthe, legally erased, lives quietly as a courier again under a new name, her found family beside her. Ashe faces trial built on the memories she surrendered. Beat: bittersweet peace — survival was paid for, but not with half of humanity.

chapters.title: The Next Long Route
chapters.summary: Epilogue. On a new run between worlds that are learning to speak again, Xanthe passes the derelict platform and leaves a marker for her original: case closed. She opens her memory file one last time and adds her own entry beneath it. Beat: continuity — she is no longer a copy of a life, but the author of one.
